newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS- FUEL OIL DOWN ON PROFIT TAKING.
newsitem.headline: ASIA PRODUCT SWAPS- FUEL OIL DOWN ON PROFIT TAKING.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps edged down late afternoon on Thursday on profit-taking as the market failed to breach the $105.00-per-tonne resistance level, traders said.
"The $105.00 resistance mark is not easy to break. Alot people came out to take profit at around this level," one trader said.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $104.75/$105.00 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $104.00/$105.00, brokers said.
But the lastest level is well below the traded highs of $105.00 and $105.25 done this morning, they said.
The sell-off of the front month also moved the market back to its established contango with October last quoted at $105.00/$105.25 from Wednesday's $104.50/$105.50 in quiet trade.
"There's a small 25 cents contango right now but the market is veering towards flat," one trader said.
Traders said the profit taking was inevitable as the swaps market has risen by over $2.50 per tonne since the start of this week and some players are of the opinion that the market was overbought.

But the physical market remains tight with the steep backwardation is still seen in the bunker market where supplies for lifting over the next few days are priced at up to $5.00 per tonne above the usual products that are sold for delivery 7-10 days out.
In the cargo market on Wednesday, a Dutch trader bid for a 20,000 tonnes of fuel oil for lifting September 8-12 but no selling interest emerged against it.
Over the past week, a Singapore trader and a Middle East trader have bought 20,000-tonne cargoes at $103.50 and $102.50 per tonne, respectively, on a free-on-board basis.
The gas oil market is steady in the absence of fresh indicators in fairly quiet trade.
September was last quoted unchanged from Wednesday at $23.30/$23.40 per barrel with one lots traded at $23.33, brokers said.
Naphtha also rose with the crude market with September last quoted at $21.40/$21.60 per barrel, up from Wednesday's $21.30/$21.40, brokers said.
September traded on Wednesday at $21.40 and $21.55, they said.
